x: Install Mentor Heart, register with your D.No. or staff ID, and learn the main screens.

k: install download start begin first time new join sign up register account approve approval wait login sign in
x: Mentor Heart is for the students and professors of a department. Only people on the department’s list can register. The department admin checks and approves each new account. This keeps strangers out.

k: install download android google play store apk iphone computer laptop web browser
x: Choose the one for your phone: Android phone: install Mentor Heart from Google Play. It updates itself. iPhone: there is no App Store app. Use the web app at mh.inigo.co.in and add it to your Home Screen. See how. Computer: open mh.inigo.co.in in any browser and sign in. Some people installed the Android app from the APK file on this website. That app still works, and it updates itself from Settings › Updates. You don’t need to change anything.

k: apk not installed invalid package problem parsing the package parse error app not installed conflicts with an existing package corrupt download failed android version old phone storage space
x: Does your phone say App not installed, Invalid package or There was a problem parsing the package? Check these, one by one: Your Android version. The app needs Android 7.0 or newer. To check, open your phone’s Settings › About phone and look at Android version. On Android 6 or older, the app can’t install. Use the web app at mh.inigo.co.in instead. It does nearly everything the app does. Mentor Heart from Google Play. Is Mentor Heart already on the phone from Google Play? Then the APK can’t replace it. Keep the Play Store app; it updates itself. To use the APK instead, uninstall the Play Store app first. Your records are safe on the server, but save your Calm journal first with Save a backup file. The download. The file must be complete. Open this website in Chrome, not inside WhatsApp or Instagram, and download the APK again. It is about 55 MB. A file sent on WhatsApp can arrive broken,

k: sign up new account dno d.no register number roll number not on the list
x: First, your D.No. must be on your department’s list. Your professors or the admin add it. Open Mentor Heart and tap New here? Register. Under I am a, tap Student. Choose your Department. Then find Your D.No. in the list. Your class is filled in for you. Type your Full name as in college records. Make a Password with at least 8 letters or numbers. Type your Mobile number. Email is optional. Only your professors see it. Add your Date of birth. If you are under 18, also add a Parent or guardian name and mobile. You can add a Profile photo and a few lines in About you. This helps your mentor. Tick I agree that my department keeps these details for mentoring and academic work. Then send the form. Your D.No. is not in the list? It may not be added yet. Or someone already used it. Ask your class professor or the department admin.

k: staff id initials staff list designation not on the list new to the department
x: Tap New here? Register. Under I am a, tap Professor. Choose your Department. Then choose Your name on the staff list. If your name is not there, choose I am not on the list. Type your Staff ID, for example 20CBU51. You sign in with it. Type your Initials as they appear on the timetable, for example IPV. This links you to your hours. Add your full name, a password (at least 8 characters), your mobile number and your Designation. Then agree and send. If your staff ID is different from the one on the staff list, the app tells you. Check it, or ask the admin.

k: new department code founding create department become admin not listed
x: Is your department not in Mentor Heart yet? One of its professors sets it up. That professor becomes its first admin. Ask the app’s owner for the new-department code (write to Inigo from the home page). The code stops strangers from making departments. Register as a professor. Under Department, choose My department is not listed. Type the Department name, the Short name (for example BBA) and the College. Then type the code. Is your department in the list but it says No admin yet? Choose it. Turn on Make me this department’s admin. Then type the department code from the owner.

k: pending waiting approve check again rejected turned off not approved
x: After you register, you see three steps: Registered, Admin approves, You’re in. The admin usually approves you within a day. Tap Check again to see if you are approved. Not approved: speak to the department office. Turned off: your account was switched off. Speak to the department office.

k: login log in password dno staff id forgot
x: Type your D.No. or staff ID and your Password. Then tap Sign in. Forgot your password? There is no email reset. Ask the department admin. They can give you a new password.

k: tabs bottom bar navigation menu more introduction tour help
x: There are five tabs at the bottom of the app: Today: today’s day order, the class now, and the next class. Calendar: the day order of each date, and events, exams and holidays. Timetable: your class’s week, or the hours you teach. Mentoring: your mentor, or your mentees. More: everything else. Leave, studies, announcements, settings and help. The first time you open the app, it shows a short introduction. To see it again, open More › Settings › Show the introduction again. There is also help inside the app, in More › Help.

t: What you can do, by role
k: role roles who what can i do permissions access rights
x: Each person sees a different Mentor Heart: students, professors, mentors, class reps, admins, heads of department, the Principal and the app’s owner. Start with your role.

t: What you can do, by role
p: What you can do, by role
k: role roles who what can i do permissions access rights
x: One person can have more than one role. Most professors are also mentors. An admin is always a professor. A head of department may or may not be an admin.

p: What you can do, by role
k: student undergraduate
x: You see your day, your mentor and your own records. You never see a classmate’s marks, attendance, leave, meetings or goals. See today’s day order and classes, the calendar and your class’s timetable. Ask your mentor for a meeting. Or tell them “I need to talk”. Tick off tasks from meetings. Set goals and check in each week. Apply for leave or on-duty. Hand in assignments. Open study materials. Keep your attendance and certificates. Read announcements and answer polls. Register for events and rate them. Use the calm space. Choose who sees your birthday.

p: What you can do, by role
k: teacher staff faculty
x: Today shows your next class. A reminder comes 5 minutes before it. See your own hours. Edit the hours you teach. Change a class for one day. Set assignments and give marks. Share study materials. Take a mock roll. Post announcements and polls. Add events. Find blood donors and the department’s people. Look after the electives you teach. Add D.No.s to the people lists.

p: What you can do, by role
k: mentees mentoring
x: A mentor is a professor. The admin gives each mentor a group of students, called mentees. “Needs you” shows meeting requests, worries, leave to decide, and mentees you have not heard from. Plan and record meetings. Write a summary for the student, and private notes for yourself only. Agree tasks. Follow goals and check-ins. Decide leave. Hold a group meeting. Share a mentee’s record as a PDF.

p: What you can do, by role
k: class representative cr rep badge
x: The admin can choose up to two class representatives for each class. You can post announcements to your own class. You can’t add pictures or pin posts. Your posts show a gold Class rep badge. Your card in More shows it too. Everything else is the same as for other students.

p: What you can do, by role
k: department admin administrator
x: The admin is a professor who looks after the department in the app. A department can have more than one admin. Approve new accounts and reset passwords. Keep the people lists, classes and class reps, mentor allotments, the day order and bell timings up to date. Edit any class’s timetable and subjects. See the department dashboard and the mentoring report. Run the best student award. Name a head of department. Start a new academic year.

p: What you can do, by role
k: hod head of department
x: The owner or a department admin names the head of department. Being head gives you one thing: the department dashboard. You can look but not change anything. You can also make PDF reports. Being head does not make you an admin. That is a different switch. Open it from More › Department dashboard, or from Today. Students: shared attendance, goals, certificates, meetings and leave. Classes: today’s classes and each professor’s hours in a week. Mentoring: who mentors whom, and how often mentees meet their mentor.

p: What you can do, by role
k: principal college overview viewer
x: The app’s owner can let the Principal, or an HoD, see the college overview. It shows numbers for every department. It never shows names or notes. Open it from More › College overview. You can share it as a PDF.

p: What you can do, by role
k: owner inigo
x: The owner looks after Mentor Heart for the whole college: department codes, heads of department, the college view, the college calendar, college-wide events and backups.

k: home start day order now next class poster dashboard
x: The first tab. It shows today’s day order, the class now, the next class, and anything that needs you.

k: home start day order now next class poster dashboard
x: When you open the app, you see Today. You can read it in two seconds.

k: day order a b c d e f 1 2 3 4 5 6 weekday holiday shift
x: The college uses day orders (A to F, or 1 to 6), not weekdays. After a holiday, the next working day takes the next day order. Today always shows the right day order. Each day order has its own colour. A yellow (marigold) day has no classes. Red means an exam, or a problem.

k: current class next class room professor poster progress
x: The coloured box at the top shows: the class now, with its room and professor; how much of the class is over; the Next class. Tap it to see the whole day, with any changes for today. Below it, you see the day orders of this week and Today’s classes. A cancelled class has a line through it, with the reason. For example, “Professor on leave”.

k: birthday exam countdown attendance reminder feedback check in mentor goal blood group cards
x: Today also shows small cards when they matter: Exam countdown: days left to your next exam. A birthday: yours, or a classmate’s or professor’s who shares it. See Birthdays. Attendance below 80%: a reminder, if you use My attendance. Check in: your weekly goal check-in. See Goals. How was the seminar?: asks you to rate an event. Your mentor: your next meeting, or No meeting booked. Announcements: the newest posts from your professors. Turn on notifications: only in the web app, until you turn them on. Tap Not now to hide a card.

k: professor today next class teaching reminder five minutes meeting requests registrations
x: Professors see their next class from all the classes they teach. A reminder comes 5 minutes before. (You can turn it off in Settings.) You also see: Meeting requests that are Waiting for a time from you. Students who wrote “I need to talk”, and leave waiting for you. New registrations, for the admin, Waiting for you to approve. Announcements, with a Post button. Coming up: events in the next few days.

t: Today for the head of department
x: If you are head of department but not an admin, Today shows a Department dashboard card. It is also in More. Department dashboard See Department dashboard.

k: offline no internet data slow saved copy pull refresh
x: Today, Timetable and Calendar keep the last copy you saw. So they open without internet. A note shows how old the copy is. When you are online again, pull the screen down to refresh it.

k: calendar month list date day order events exam holiday deadline meeting dots key
x: Every date with its day order, and the department’s events, exams, holidays, deadlines and meetings.

k: month list view dots colours key legend
x: Open the Calendar tab. At the top, choose Month or List. Use the arrows to change the month. Each date shows its day order letter, in that day’s colour. Today’s date is filled with colour. A holiday is yellow. Tap Key below the month to see what each mark means. Dots under a date show what is on that day: Mark Meaning Pink dot An event Red dot An exam Yellow dot A holiday Blue dot A deadline Violet dot A meeting Small pink ring A birthday

k: day page classes on a date
x: Tap a date. Its events show below the month. Tap Classes to see that day’s timetable, with any changes. Tap Today to come back to today.

k: who decides day order college calendar holiday changes count
x: The college calendar decides the day order of each date. The app’s owner puts it into the app for the whole college. A department admin can also change one date, for example a day with no classes. See Day order for admins.

k: event exam holiday register
x: Tap an event to open it. You see the time, the place, the details, a poster and links. Some events ask you to register. Professors add events with Add event. See Events. You get a reminder the evening before an event, and an hour before. Turn this on or off in Settings › Event reminders.

Some events are for the whole college, such as exams and holidays. Every department sees them. Only the app’s owner can change them. Staff and committee meetings are for professors only. Students don’t see them.

k: timetable schedule hours periods class week day subjects elective dse generic sec change cancel extra
x: Your class’s week by day order, a professor’s own hours, changes for one day, subjects and electives.

k: day week view swipe grid subject codes
x: Open the Timetable tab. Day shows one day order. Swipe left or right to see the others. Week shows all six day orders in one table. The subject codes are explained below it. Students see their own class. Breaks show between the periods.

k: my hours teaching hours professor not on the staff list link account
x: Professors can tap My hours to see every hour they teach, in all classes. Or tap Class to see any class’s timetable. Does the app say You are not on the staff list? Then your account is not linked to your name yet. Open More › People lists › Staff. Tap your name and choose Link to an account. Or ask the admin.

t: Change a class for one day
k: cancel class change room extra class one day only professor on leave substitute special timings half day exam day
x: You can change a class for one date only. The weekly timetable does not change. Tap the date on the Calendar, then tap Classes. Or tap the coloured box on Today. Tap a period. Choose Cancelled, Changed or Extra class. Add a Reason or a Note for the class. For example, “Professor on leave” or “In the computer lab”. Tap Save for this day. Students see the change at once. To undo it, tap the period again and choose Back to the usual class. Different bell timings for one day (a half day or an exam day): on the same page, tap Change this day’s timings, then Save timings for this day. To go back, tap Use the usual timings.

k: edit timetable weekly admin professor own hours bell timings
x: Professors can edit the hours they teach. The admin can edit every hour. Open Timetable. Choose the class and tap Edit the weekly timetable. Tap an hour. Tap a subject from the class’s list. This fills in the subject, the professor and the room. Or type them yourself. Tap Save. If you type a new subject, it is added to the class’s list of subjects. Does the app say The admin has not set up the periods yet? Then the admin must first add the bell timings.

k: subjects list taught by room hours grid quickest way fill timetable
x: This is the quickest way to fill a class’s timetable. Open Timetable › Subjects for the class. Add each subject, with who teaches it and the room. Open a subject. You see a table: day orders A to F down the side, periods across the top. Tap the hours when this subject is taught. Hours of other subjects show their code. Save. If this takes an hour from another subject or another professor, the app tells you first. If you change a subject’s professor or room, the app asks if its hours should change too.

k: elective dse generic elective ge sec skill enhancement other department group
x: An elective is a group with its own hours and its own students. For example, a DSE taken by students from two sections. Or a generic elective with students from other departments. Students see their own elective group in that hour, with its room and professor. An hour taught by another department (for example Tamil or English): tap it to add the subject, the room and the teacher. Only you see this. Professors and the admin manage electives in More › Electives. Add students (your own students by class, and outside students as “D.No. Name”). Set the hours. Professors of an elective can change its students and hours.
Professors get a notification 5 minutes before each class they teach. To turn it off, open Settings › Class reminders. These reminders work without internet.

k: announcement post notice news poll vote pin schedule badge admin class rep picture link
x: Read the department’s posts and answer polls. Professors post to everyone, to a class or to their mentees. A class rep posts to their own class.

k: read posts notices pinned picture link badge
x: Open More › Announcements. The newest ones also show on Today. Pinned posts stay at the top. Tap a picture to see it bigger. Tap a link to open it. A blue Admin badge means the post is from the department admin. A gold Class rep badge means the post is from your class representative.

k: vote poll answer results counts change vote anonymous
x: Some announcements ask a question. Tap an answer to vote. After you vote, you see how many people chose each answer. You can change your vote while the announcement is still up. Nobody can see who voted for what. Not even the professor who asked.

k: post write new announcement everyone class mentees professors only pin picture links schedule remove after poll
x: Open More › Announcements and tap Post. (Or tap Post on Today.) Write a Title and a Message. Choose who it is for: Everyone, One class, My mentees or Professors only. You can add one picture (a poster or invitation) and up to six links. Send it. Everyone it is for gets a notification. You can also: Pin to top: keep it above newer posts. Schedule: choose a Day and Time to send it later. Nobody sees it before then. Remove after a day: choose the Last day it shows. Add a poll: a Question with up to six answers. Big files (PDFs, videos, many photos) should go on Google Drive or YouTube. Then add the link. Links don’t use the app’s free storage. To change or delete a post, open its menu. Choose Edit or Delete.

k: class representative rep post own class
x: Are you a class representative? Then you can post to your own class. Open More › Announcements › Post. Class reps can’t add pictures or pin posts. Your posts show a gold Class rep badge.
The admin chooses up to two class representatives for each class. Open More › Classes and sections, open the class, and choose Class representatives. See Admin tools.

k: event seminar webinar workshop field visit activity register registration place limit feedback rating poster
x: Seminars, workshops, field visits, exams and holidays on the calendar. Register, get reminders and give feedback.

k: event page details poster venue links
x: Tap an event on the Calendar, or under Coming up on Today. You see: the date and time, and the Venue (the place); the details, a poster and links; who it is for: Whole department, one class, Professors only, or Whole college, from the college calendar.

k: register sign up cancel registration full place limit closed
x: Some events ask you to register. Open the event. Tap Register for this event. The page now says You are registered. Changed your mind? Tap Cancel registration. You can register again while registration is open. Some events have a limit on places. When all places are taken, it says This event is full. After registration closes, it says Registration has closed.

k: feedback rate rating stars seminar how was it
x: After some events (a seminar, webinar, workshop, field visit or activity), Today asks How was the seminar? Tap a star to rate it, from 1 to 5. If you want, write a few words under Anything to add? Send it. You can change it until a week after the event. Your name and class go with your feedback.
You get a reminder the evening before an event that is for you, and an hour before. To turn this off, open Settings › Event reminders.

k: add new event create exam holiday deadline meeting professors only no classes registration place limit
x: Open Calendar and tap Add event. Type the Title. Choose the kind: event, exam, holiday, deadline, meeting, or Something else. Choose the Date. For an event over many days, also choose Ends on. Type the Venue. Under Who is it for?, choose the whole department or one class. For staff meetings, turn on Professors only. You can add a poster and links. Tap Add to calendar. The people it is for get a notification. Other switches: Students can register: adds a Register button. You can set a Place limit. Leave it empty for no limit. Ask students for feedback: for a seminar, webinar, workshop, field visit or activity. No classes on these days: also marks these dates as days with no classes.

t: See who registered, and the feedback
k: registrations list excel who registered feedback results pdf
x: On the event page, Who registered shows the list of students. Tap Share as Excel to get the list as a spreadsheet. If the event asked for feedback, the page shows the average rating. Open it to read the answers class by class, and to see who has not answered. You can save it as a PDF or Excel file. All professors and admins of the department can read the feedback.

k: notification notifications alert alerts reminder reminders push sound not coming not arriving missing turn on off
x: Choose which notifications you get. Find out what to do when they don’t come.

k: notification notifications alert alerts reminder reminders push sound not coming not arriving missing turn on off
x: Mentor Heart sends two kinds of notification: From your department: announcements, new events, mentoring, leave and tasks. These need internet. Reminders on this phone: before classes, events, deadlines and meetings. The phone makes these itself, so they work without internet.

k: settings choose which kinds turn off announcements events mentoring leave tasks class reminders event reminders
x: Open More › Settings › Notifications. Turn each kind on or off. Setting Students Professors Class reminders – 5 minutes before each class you teach Event reminders The evening before, and an hour before – Tasks, goals and meetings Before something is due, and before meetings – Meetings and leave – Before meetings, and at 9 am when leave is waiting Announcements, New events, Leave Yes Yes Mentoring Meetings with your mentor Requests, worries and late tasks Tasks New tasks from your mentor – Tap Send a test notification to check that notifications reach you.
Mentors also get a note when a mentee’s task is two days late. Every Monday, they get a note with what needs them that week.

k: not working not coming missing silent blocked battery
x: In the app, open Settings › Notifications. Tap Send a test notification. Does the app say Notifications are off for Mentor Heart in your phone’s settings? Tap Open phone settings and allow notifications. Check that the kind you want is turned on in the app. Some phones stop apps to save battery. In your phone’s settings, let Mentor Heart run with no battery limit. Open the app from time to time. It gets anything new when you open it. On an iPhone, notifications only work when the web app is on your Home Screen. See iPhone and computers.

k: mentor mentee mentoring meeting request schedule log notes private tasks goals habits check in streak concern talk group record pdf
x: Meetings, “I need to talk”, tasks, goals and weekly check-ins, for students and their mentors.

k: mentor mentee mentoring meeting request schedule log notes private tasks goals habits check in streak concern talk group record pdf
x: Every student has a professor as their mentor. The department admin chooses the mentor. Everything between you and your mentor is in the Mentoring tab.

t: Ask your mentor for a meeting
k: request meeting ask to meet book appointment
x: Open Mentoring and tap Ask to meet. Under What would you like to talk about?, write a few words. This helps your mentor get ready. Tap Send request. Your mentor chooses a time. You get a notification, and a reminder an hour before the meeting. To cancel your request, open it and tap Withdraw request. Does it say You do not have a mentor yet? The admin has not given you a mentor. Ask the department office.

k: concern worried problem urgent help talk private
x: Use this when something is wrong and you can’t wait for the next meeting. Open Mentoring and tap I need to talk. Choose what it is about: studies, personal, health, money, career, or something else. Choose how soon: When you can, This week or Today, please. You can add a few words. Then tap Tell my mentor. Only your mentor sees it. Your mentor will contact you.

k: tasks to do agreed tick off due late
x: In a meeting, you and your mentor can agree on tasks. Each task has a due date. Students see them under To do from your meetings. Tick each task when it is done. You get a reminder the evening before it is due, and on the morning it is due. Mentors add tasks when they record a meeting (Tasks agreed, one task per line). Or tap Add task on a mentee’s page. If a task is two days late, the mentor gets a note.

k: goal habit semester target streak check in weekly progress steps private shared
x: Open More › Goals. Or open Goals and habits on the Mentoring tab. Tap New goal. Choose Goal: finish it (something to finish, like “Score above 75% in Accounts”) or Habit: keep it up (something to do every day, like “Revise for 30 minutes”). You can add How will you know it’s done?, By when? and First steps (one step per line). Share with my mentor is on. Your mentor sees the goal and can encourage you. Turn it off to keep the goal private. For a habit, tick it each day you do it. If you forgot to tick a day, tap that day to fix it. Check in each week: tap Check in. Choose how the week went, from Stuck to Great. Add a few words. Each week in a row adds to your streak. You can also set a daily reminder for a goal.

k: needs you mentees list requests concerns quiet not met checked in due
x: Open Mentoring. Needs you shows what is waiting: meeting requests; students who wrote “I need to talk”; leave to decide; mentees you have not met for a while, or who stopped checking in. Below it you see Coming up (your next meetings) and My mentees. Tap a mentee to open their page. It shows meetings, your private notes, tasks, their shared goals and check-ins, their attendance (if they share it) and their certificates. You can also tap Call student or Call guardian.

k: schedule meeting set a time log held summary
x: To answer a request: tap it and choose Set a time. Choose the Date, Time and Place. Your mentee sees the time. To plan a meeting yourself: tap Schedule a meeting. After the meeting: open it. Fill in Held on, the Summary (the student sees this), Tasks agreed and Private notes (only you see these). For a meeting you did not plan in the app: tap Log a meeting on the mentee’s page.

k: private notes confidential who can see mentor only
x: Only the mentor can read their private notes. Not the student. Not the admin. Not the head of department. Private notes are never in a report, a PDF or a backup. The student sees only the Summary.

k: check in rhythm nudge quiet how often
x: On a mentee’s page, choose how often you want them to check in. If a mentee stops checking in, you can send a friendly reminder (a nudge). The student’s Today shows the check-in card at the times you chose.

k: group meeting several mentees together
x: Tap Group meeting on the Mentoring tab. Or, when you record a meeting, tap Add other mentees (group meeting). The meeting, the summary and the tasks go on each student’s record. Private notes stay separate for each student.

t: Share a mentee’s record as a PDF
k: record pdf naac parents meeting print share
x: On a mentee’s page, tap Share record as PDF. The PDF has their meetings, tasks and shared goals. Use it for NAAC files or a parents’ meeting. Private notes are never in it.
The admin can see a report of meetings for each mentor and mentee in More › Mentoring report. See Admin tools.

k: studies assignment homework hand in submit marks grade materials notes pdf attendance percentage 75 certificate wallet mock roll
x: Assignments and marks, study materials, your attendance, your certificates, and mock attendance for professors.

k: studies assignment homework hand in submit marks grade materials notes pdf attendance percentage 75 certificate wallet mock roll
x: Students find these in More › Studies. Professors find them in More › Department. Assignments Study materials My attendance My certificates

k: hand in submit upload photo pdf assignment due seen redo paper
x: Open More › Assignments. You see the assignments for your class and your electives. The one due first is at the top. You get a notification when a new one is set. Open the assignment. Tap Add a photo or PDF. Take a photo of each page (up to six pages). Or choose a PDF file of up to 5 MB. Hand it in. It says Handed in. Your professor can see it now. You can change it until your professor marks it Seen. If your professor marks it Please redo, you can hand it in again. Some assignments are handed in on paper. Your professor ticks your name when you give it. Files are deleted one month after they are marked. This keeps the app free. Keep your own copy. Your marks stay.

k: marks score out of result grade remark
x: Some assignments have marks, for example “Out of 10”. When your professor gives your marks, they show on the assignment, with any remark. You get a notification.

k: set assignment new due date class elective out of marks
x: Open More › Assignments and tap Set an assignment. Type the Subject, the Title and What to do. Choose the class or elective, and the Due on date. Choose how students hand it in: In the app or On paper. If you will give marks, fill in Out of. Save it. Students get a notification.

k: mark seen redo enter marks paper excel who handed in
x: In the app: open each hand-in. Mark it Seen or Please redo, and add a remark if you want. The student gets a notification. On paper: tap each student when they give it to you. Tap again to undo. Marks: give marks to each student one by one. Or tap Enter marks to give marks for the whole class at once. For paper assignments, giving marks also ticks the student as handed in. Share as Excel gives a list of who handed in and who did not, with dates, marks and remarks. Hand-in files are deleted 30 days after you mark them. The record of who handed in stays.

k: materials notes pdf video link drive youtube subject
x: Open More › Study materials. You find notes, videos and PDFs by subject, for your class or elective. Professors tap Add to add a Google Drive or YouTube link, or a PDF of up to 5 MB. Links are better: they cost nothing to store.

k: attendance percentage 75 80 hours held attended bunk miss shortage
x: The college keeps the real attendance. This page helps you see where you stand. Open More › My attendance. Look at the college’s attendance page. Type the Hours held and the Hours attended, and the date (As of). Tap Save. The app shows your percentage. It also tells you how many hours you can miss and still stay at 75%. Or how many hours you must attend to get back to 75%. If you go below 80%, Today shows a reminder. My mentor can see it is on at first. Your mentor can then help early if your attendance drops. If you share it, the head of department and the admins can also see it on the department dashboard. If you turn it off, nobody else sees it.

k: certificate wallet course nss sports internship event photo pdf
x: Open More › My certificates and tap Add. Add a photo or PDF of each certificate: courses, events, NSS, sports, internships. The app suggests events you took part in. Your mentor and the admin can see your certificates. They are deleted one month after you finish college. Keep your own copies.

k: mock attendance roll call absent present college system down excel pdf
x: Use this when the college’s attendance system is not working. Open More › Mock attendance and tap Take attendance. Choose the class, date and period. Everyone starts as present. Tap only the students who are absent. Share it as a CSV file (opens in Excel) or a PDF. The list stays on your phone. It is not sent to the department.
